title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND
description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

title: Game Night @ Archetype Brewing
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Birding for Beginners
description:
Birding for Beginners
with Shane Myers 
Tuesday, December 1  |  9 – 10:30am 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Join us on this birding walk around the NC Arboretum gardens and trails in search of our most colorful residents. We will go over best practices for using binoculars, recommendations for purchasing your own binoculars, and popular field guides to use. Bring your own binoculars but if you do not have a pair we have some loaner binoculars available to use during the programs. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**December 2026 Selection - *When Breach Becomes Air* by Paul Kalanithi**
[Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/When-Breath-Becomes-Paul-Kalanithi/dp/081298840X/) - [GoodReads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/25899336-when-breath-becomes-)

*At the age of thirty-six, on the verge of completing a decade’s worth of training as a neurosurgeon, Paul Kalanithi was diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer. One day he was a doctor treating the dying, and the next he was a patient struggling to live. And just like that, the future he and his wife had imagined evaporated. When Breath Becomes Air chronicles Kalanithi’s transformation from a naïve medical student “possessed,” as he wrote, “by the question of what, given that all organisms die, makes a virtuous and meaningful life” into a neurosurgeon at Stanford working in the brain, the most critical place for human identity, and finally into a patient and new father confronting his own mortality.*

*What makes life worth living in the face of death? What do you do when the future, no longer a ladder toward your goals in life, flattens out into a perpetual present? What does it mean to have a child, to nurture a new life as another fades away? These are some of the questions Kalanithi wrestles with in this profoundly moving, exquisitely observed memoir.*

*Paul Kalanithi died in March 2015, while working on this book, yet his words live on as a guide and a gift to us all. “I began to realize that coming face to face with my own mortality, in a sense, had changed nothing and everything,” he wrote. “Seven words from Samuel Beckett began to repeat in my head: ‘I can’t go on. I’ll go on.’” When Breath Becomes Air is an unforgettable, life-affirming reflection on the challenge of facing death and on the relationship between doctor and patient, from a brilliant writer who became both.*

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

**Welcome to our monthly Book Club!** We’re a small, friendly group that gets together for fun, thoughtful conversations about a different book each month.

Finished the whole book? Great. Only made it through a few chapters? Still come. Didn’t read it at all but the discussion sounds interesting? Honestly, you’re welcome too.
We meet on the **first Tuesday of every month**.

One of the best things about this group is that we keep it relatively small and guide the conversation, so it doesn’t turn into three people talking while everyone else quietly questions their life choices. Everyone has a chance to jump in, share their thoughts, and explore the book’s characters, themes, writing, and bigger ideas.

You definitely don’t need to be a literary expert. Whether you read constantly or you’re trying to get back into it, this is a relaxed place to discover new books, hear different perspectives, and meet some great people along the way.

title: Handmade Holiday: Wild Ornaments
description:
Handmade Holiday: Wild Ornaments
with Carleigh Fairchild 
Wednesday, December 2  |  10 am – 1 pm 
Register Here!
Using cattail leaves and colored ribbons we will make several different styles of ornaments: animal shapes and star shapes. 
Previous basket making or weaving experience is not necessary but you will use fine motor skills to make these ornaments. You will have the opportunity to make many during our time together, to decorate your tree or to give as gifts. All materials are provided in this class. 
Carleigh Fairchild has a deep love for the Earth. She gardens, keeps bees, wild harvests, processes animals, tans hides, weaves baskets, and finds joy in time spent around the fire. As the founder of Human Nature Connection LLC, she is dedicated to helping others rediscover respectful and collaborative relationships with the more then human world. Carleigh’s journey—including 86 days on the survival show ALONE in Patagonia—deepened her understanding of belonging and connection. With over 25 years of experience, she teaches both online and in-person classes in Western North Carolina, weaving together earth skills, community, and healing. Carleigh is also a NIASZIIH bodywork healer and instructor at Wilderness Fusion, integrating body, earth, and spirit in her practice.

title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

title: Meet Gracie! Read to a Therapy Dog
location: Enka-Candler Library - 1404 Sandhill Rd. - Candler
description: Location: Enka-Candler Library - 1404 Sandhill Rd. - CandlerPhone: (828) 250-4758Email: enka.library@buncombecounty.orgEvent Type: Family Fun,STEM/STEAM,Story TellingAge Group: Toddler - (ages 18 mos.-2 yrs.),Preschool - (ages 3-5),School Age - (grades K-5),Family - (children of all ages)Library: Enka-CandlerLink: https://www.buncombecounty.org/governing/depts/library/branch-locations/enka-candler.aspxMeet Gracie, a certified therapy dog whose spirit and affectionate personality are sure to win your heart. Despite having one less leg, this ten year old "tripod" Great Pyrenees mix is excited about life, always eager for a run or swim and approaches everything with a big smile. Gracie's physical difference does not stop her mission to spread love and happiness to everyone she meets. Her empathy and willingness to listen, make her the perfect friend for anyone in need of comfort or support.Join Gracie and her parent, Lisa, for an hour at the library where you can take turns reading, petting, or saying hello! title: Thursday Run
description:
Asheville Runners
Come run 1, 3, or 6 miles and stay for a beer and soccer tennis after at Olde London Road.

Routes-
1 miler:
RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.
RIGHT on River Arts Place
Cross Riverside onto the Greenway
Right on the Greenway to the Craven St Park put in (the dock)
Turn around and go back the same way to OLR

3 miler:
Start the same as 1 miler
Continue onto Craven St. Bridge
LEFT onto Greenway after bridge
Follow Greenway all the way until it ends at Haywood Rd.
RIGHT onto Haywood Rd, go across the bridge
Cross the Roundabout at Roberts St. and continue onto Clingman
Continue on Clingman
LEFT onto Owens Bell Lane
LEFT onto Hilliard at the top of the hill
LEFT onto W Haywood, follow all the way down to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts
Follow Roberts back to OLR
Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

6 miler:
After the W Haywood downhill to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts St. take to Lyman and head back to the Greenway
LEFT onto the Greenway, take all the way to Amboy
RIGHT on Amboy to cross the bridge
RIGHT into French Broad River Park, run the loop at the park
Cross back over the bridge on Amboy and run the Greenway back to the roundabout
Follow Lyman back to OLR

**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Handmade Holiday: Mosaic Mirror Workshop
description:
Handmade Holiday: Mosaic Mirror Workshop
with Linda Pannullo 
Friday, December 4  |  12 – 4pm 
Register Here!
All levels welcome! Learn basic mosaic techniques and create a piece of art to embellish your home. Instructor will provide 12″ substrate with an 8″ mirror. Students will decorate the 2″ border with glass, tile and other embellishments. All materials, tools, adhesives, physical handouts provided. Students may also bring jewelry, special items to add to their mirror. 
Linda Pannullo is a local mosaic artist that uses both traditional and contemporary for my art. Her work ranges from the whimsical to fine art, from eclectic materials to the traditional stained glass and 3D sculptures. She loves to teach and currently instructs at the John C Campbell Folk School in Brasstown, NC, Olive’s Porch, the Purple Crayon and Trackside Studios in Asheville. She is very fond of FUNctional Art and love bringing new folks into the mosaic world. One of her biggest honors is to be the 1st mosaic artist to exhibit at the NC Arboretum and have a permanent mosaic installation, Nature’s Throne there.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Methods of Teaching Environmental Education Workshop, NC EE Criteria I
description:
Methods of Teaching Environmental Education Workshop, NC EE Criteria I
with Michelle Pearce 
4 hours of online self-guided online learning and 
In-person Saturday, December 5  |  10 am – 4 pm 
Register Here!
The Methods of Teaching EE (MOTEE) workshop helps practitioners create inclusive and age-appropriate learning experiences, gain group management skills, practice teaching methods to promote inquiry, and gain skills in designing objectives, lessons, and assessments for EE programs using NC Essential Standards as a foundation. This will be a hybrid workshop, with 4 hours of online, self-guided learning, in addition to a 6 hour in person session. Participants will receive 10 hours of Criteria 1 credit toward their NC EE Certification. 
This program will take place both in the classroom and outside following easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the part program time. 
Michelle Pierce has worked in Environmental Education since 2007. It was actually her first job right out of college, and she fell in love with it! Michelle has been a seasonal staff, Summer camp staff, county parks staff, a state employee, an adjunct professor, and now is currently serving as the Programming Lead for the Environmental Educators of North Carolina. She has a Bachelor’s degree in Biology with an emphasis in life science, and a Masters of Arts in Education with an emphasis in Science Education. She’s been a Project Wet facilitator since 2010 and currently resides in Candler with her son and her leopard gecko.

**MENU:🍷** **To see their menu please go to: www.passerelleinthepark.com**

**In Falls Park there are trails, gardens, shops, craft beer pubs, and restaurants. The park & bridge are free and open to the public.**

title: Wild Pages: Creating Nature Zines
description:
Wild Pages: Creating Nature Zines
with Meg Worthington 
Saturday, December 5  |  1 – 4 pm 
Register Here!
Discover the creative world of zines while deepening your connection to the natural world around you. Zines are small, handmade publications that have long been used to share ideas, art, stories, and personal experiences. In this beginner-friendly workshop, participants will learn about the history and cultural significance of zines, explore examples of nature-focused zines, and create their own mini nature zine inspired by observations from the NC Arboretum. 
Through sketching, writing, collage, and simple book-folding techniques, participants will transform their observations into a unique publication they can take home. No artistic experience is necessary. This workshop is designed for adults of all skill levels and emphasizes curiosity, creativity, and careful observation. All materials will be provided, but feel free to bring in any personal art materials you may want to use. 
This class will take place primarily in a classroom, with a short portion taking place outside following easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for around 30 minutes. 
Meg Worthington (they/them) began teaching in Alaska while pursuing their Master’s degree in Outdoor and Environmental Education. While pursuing their degree they found a great sense of purpose in connecting students with the natural world and fostering a sense of curiosity and joy in learners of all ages. Meg’s experience working on a small educational farm in Palmer, Alaska helped to instill a keen interest in how we interact and cultivate our experiences within nature and our local communities. They are currently enjoying learning more about the local ecology of Western North Carolina and are excited to begin teaching classes as an Adult Education Specialist with the Adult Education Department at The NC Arboretum. Meg is also a local artist in the Asheville area, working with a variety of mediums including zines and collage to share and process the wide array of human emotions and what it means to be a soul. They love incorporating nature into their artwork and are always keen to learn new processes and artforms.

title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND
description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

title: Vaden Landers
description:
Vaden Landers is a multi-instumentalist & singer-songwriter hailing from eastern Tennessee who blends influences from honky tonk, hillbilly, folk, blues, ragtime, jazz, western swing and old-time Appalachian to bring new fire to a classic sound!



As a teen, he set out traveling the American highways & railways, learning the ways of a traveler-musician while honing his songwriting, singing, yodeling & picking skills busking & touring from Alaska to Florida.



Landers' original songs harken back to the golden days of country music and, with a voice that draws comparison to Hank Sr., he continues to turn heads as an exciting new player in the revival of the traditional country music scene.



Music from 8:30-11:30, $10 cover at the door.

title: Fantasy and Sci-Fi Silent Book Club
description:
Asheville Introverts
BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles!

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather, grab drinks and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. We want to know what you're reading! Organic dialogue welcome!

title: New Moon Ceremony
description:
Senseful Soul’s Asheville Healing Community🧘🏻‍♀️🏳️‍🌈🪐🔮
Join us for a gathering to set new intentions and connect with the energy of the new moon.
Meet the New Moon in ceremony through astrology, Akashic soul journeying, ritual & embodied intention.
Approaching the threshold of a new lunar cycle with intentionality is a powerful choice that becomes even more amplified when done in community.

The New Moon offers a monthly portal to pause, listen inward, and consciously seed what you desire to cultivate in the cycle ahead. Gathering in ceremony creates the space to step outside the momentum of everyday life and meet that threshold with presence, allowing your intentions to be witnessed, embodied, and amplified within the collective.

Each New Moon also carries the unique energetic signature of the zodiac sign it moves through, offering different themes and invitations for your growth. By working intentionally with the astrology of each lunation, you can align your intentions with the energies already available to you and receive deeper clarity around what is ready to begin.

Each month, we gather at the Soul Sanctuary beneath the dark moon sky for an evening of astrology, soul journeying, ritual, and embodied intention.

**This month with the Sagittarius New Moon, we invite you to lift your gaze toward a larger horizon and reconnect with what makes you feel alive, expansive, and full of possibility.**

**Together, we’ll work with Sagittarius’ fiery medicine to clarify the truth and vision guiding our next chapter, strengthen our faith in where we’re being called, and plant intentions that ask us to move courageously toward it.**

**What to Expect**

* Guided drop-in meditation
* Astrological teaching + transmission
* Guided Akashic soul journey
* Reflection + intention setting
* Ceremonial fire offerings
* Closing embodiment + integration
* Sacred space for connection and community

No prior experience with astrology, meditation, or ceremonial practice is necessary. Simply come as you are.

**About Your Facilitators**
Alessandra Mary is a trained priestess, ceremonialist, and Akashic guide devoted to creating spaces where the sacred becomes something you can experience, embody, and weave into everyday life.

Jenn is a witch of the cosmos and astrologer who brings the language of the stars down to earth, illuminating the energetic patterns and possibilities available within each lunar cycle.

Together, Alessandra and Jenn weave the mystical and the embodied, the cosmic and the ceremonial, creating a space where you can not only understand the energy of the New Moon, but more importantly, experience it.

**What to Bring**
Our ceremony will primarily take place outside on the grass around the fire, with a large covered porch available as our rain plan. Please dress with the evening weather in mind.

**Be sure to bring:**

* Water bottle
* Journal + pen
* Comfortable clothing and layers appropriate for the weather
* Any sacred objects, crystals, talismans, or other items you would like to place on our collective altar and charge during the ceremony

Lawn blankets and meditation cushions will be provided, though you are very welcome to bring your own blanket, cushion, or camping chair if you’d prefer.

Come ready to slow down, listen deeply, sit beneath the dark moon, and lean into what is waiting to begin.

title: The Leopard by Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa
description:
Books That Age Like Wine
**in 1860s Sicily, Don Fabrizio Corbera, Prince of Salina, remains skeptical and stoic as he faces civil war and his family's loss of wealth and status. The prince's favorite nephew, Tancredi, who opportunistically supports the unification efforts, marries Angelica, a beautiful woman from a lower social class, to secure his future. This marriage symbolizes the shifting social order and the decline of the aristocracy. As Don Fabrizio struggles to adapt, he retreats into his love of astronomy, finding solace in the unchanging stars while his world crumbles around him. Ultimately, he must decide to resist the forces of change or come to terms with them.**

**Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa, the last in a line of Sicilian princes, drew inspiration from his own family's decline to write this novel in the 1950s. The dramatic sweep and richness of Lampedusa’s observation, his seamless intertwining of public and private worlds, and his sure grasp of human frailty imbue The Leopard with beauty and power.**

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: J. Plank
description:
J. Plank (Jeff Plankenhorn) is a BC-based, internationally touring singer-songwriter and master of the lap steel guitar. Known for soulful vocals, dynamic stagecraft, and a sound that bridges roots, blues, and folk, he has spent decades captivating audiences across North America, Europe, and Japan. Plank is a highly respected musician recognized for his skill as a slide guitarist, songwriter, and vocalist, gaining acclaim both as a solo artist and as a sought-after session player. His style blends blues, folk, and roots into a sound that’s uniquely his own.



In 2025, he released The Bend, a stripped-down solo acoustic album recorded on the Texas coast, showcasing just his voice, lap steel, acoustic guitar, and piano. Later this year he will follow it with a high-energy roots rock album recorded in the Netherlands with the band The Southern Aces — a project that blends live-off-the-floor energy with wizardly guitar playing, innovative songwriting, and, most of all, deep groove.



Plank’s career includes collaborations with a wide range of artists, headline festival slots, and multiple Austin Music Award nominations for Musician of the Year, Best Guitarist, and a win for Best Misc. Instrument for “The Plank,” a hybrid lap steel guitar he designed himself. For him, music is about bringing people together — whether biker or drag queen, listener or dancer — to share in the joy and connection that only a great song can deliver...



Join him on his first performance at Jack of the Wood, along with a local Asheville band backing up every note. This is a show you shouldn't miss. Music 8:30-11:30pm $10 cover at the door.

Join us for our monthly project/co-working day! Bring your own project for co-working or jump in on an existing project. We can use all different kinds of support, from emailing to data entry to coding.

**Location:**
Hi Wire Brewing - Biltmore Village / Guajiro Cuban food truck
2A Huntsman Pl, Asheville, NC 28803

**What to expect:**
(Feel free to drop in when you can and leave when you need to.)

* *11am*: Arrival and introductions. Say hi and catch up with your Code with Asheville crew.
* *11:15-11:30am*: Folks chat through what they hope to accomplish for the day, ask for help, and divide into small groups for certain projects. This is a great place to get plugged in if you're looking for a project to work on.

title: Game Night @ Archetype Brewing
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Omni Grove Park Inn & Spa /Annual National Gingerbread House Competition ~ FREE!
description:
Senior Singles Fun Bunch
**The National Gingerbread House Competition is a nationally recognized competition and display at the Omni Grove Park Inn & Spa. Admission is FREE. The display of gingerbread houses features whimsical and elaborate handmade gingerbread houses of every size, shape, complexity, and theme. A must-see! You will see everything from rustic cabins to elaborate castles — all built from edible materials and made of at least 75% gingerbread. Contestants from all over the country submit their creations from across four age categories ~ adult, teen, youth, and child.**

**Besides seeing the gingerbread houses enjoy the enormous fireplaces, dozens of decorated Christmas trees with different themes, and the historic beauty of the Grove Park Inn. Also, treat yourself to their homemade hot chocolate or a hot toddy from the bar. That’s what I plan on doing! I want a hot-buttered rum and to sit in one of the rocking chairs in front of one of those huge fireplaces! Ahhhh! 🔥 🍹Come join me!**

**To read more about all that is offered at the Inn google The National Gingerbread House Competition for there are many articles and beautiful photos of gingerbread houses. You can also go to: www.omnihotels.com.**

**PUBLIC VIEWING:** **👀** **Unless you’re a registered guest of the hotel the gingerbread houses can only be viewed Monday-Thursday. That’s why our meetup is not scheduled for the weekend.**

**PETS: 🐶** **Only pets of registered guests are allowed.**

**PARKING: 🅿️** **Admission is free, but parking certainly isn’t!**
**Valet: $40 for day parking.**
**Self-parking: $30 for day parking.**
**The proceeds from parking benefits local non-profits.**

**CARPOOLING: 🚗** **I encourage carpooling due to the price of parking. If you’re willing to do so please comment in the comment section for this meetup event. Please leave contact info.**

**DAWN/CARPOOLING: 🚙** **Dawn has a nice-size Flex Ford and can accept five passengers. The first five to respond get the seats! We will be doing the valet parking for $40 plus tip. Split seven ways (that includes Dawn & me) it will be about $7-$8 per person. Beats paying the whole $40!**
**If you wish to carpool with Dawn please text me (please no phone calls for I work and my phone will be off) or email me. All others who wish to let others ride with them please make a comment in the comment section. My contact information is at bottom.**
**For those riding with Dawn we will be meeting up at IHOP Restaurant on Airport Rd. Please read the separate meetup event for IHOP. Dawn & I will be having breakfast there prior to leaving for the Grove Park Inn. Come join us or just come before we depart (Again, for details please look at the separate meetup event for IHOP). I know this is a lot of information so please text or email me with any questions.**

**DINING:🍴I tried to get dining at the Inn, but for a large group they now require you to pay in advance for everyone with only one credit card. No can do. I also wanted the Sunset Terrace, but they close in early November. Several of the restaurants are seasonal. But if you want something to eat while there they do serve food at their many on-site bars & restaurants (that are not seasonal).**

**Again, please text or email me (info. below) if you wish to carpool (first come, first serve) with Dawn or if you simply have some questions.**

**WHERE TO MEET ME:** **For those NOT carpooling with Dawn I will meet you inside the main entrance/lobby of the Inn at 11:30 AM. I’ll be in the area of one of the two huge fireplaces ~ preferably the one where I can get a rocker in front of the fireplace. 🔥 Text or call me if you can’t find me. (828)699-8180. Hope to see you there! Tis the season! 🎄 🎄🎄**

**QUESTIONS?**
**Shae ~ (828)699-8180**
**Shae.Kemerer@aol.com**

title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

description:

Led by Founding teacher Ronya Banks or AIM Facilitator Wallace Bohanan, our Thursday evening group meditation sessions will continue to consist of a guided meditation (30 minutes), a few-minute break, a dharma talk by the teacher (30 minutes), and then Q & A/Discussion (30 minutes).

Meditation instructions will be given for beginners.

The session begins promptly at 7:00 pm. If online, please mute your audio during the guided meditation and talk.

Location

MindSpring Building
966 Tunnel Road, Asheville, NC 28805

Group Meditation Guidelines

* Arrive several minutes early. You are welcome to greet others before we start.
* Turn off your cell phones and other beeping devices.
* Sit in a comfortable position, chairs are provided, bring your own cushions, blankets, or props.
* If on zoom, please mute yourself during guided meditation, and talk, and then unmute yourself to share during the discussion.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Gaming Night @ Noble Cider
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
Roll the dice and pour a glass! 🎲🍎

Gaming Night is back at Noble Cider! Join us every other Tuesday for a night of tabletop tactics, card-shuffling chaos, and great company. Whether you’re a seasoned strategist or you still think a "meeple" is a type of small fruit, you’re welcome at our table.

### The Lowdown:

* **No Experience? No Problem:** We’re all about community. We’ll help you learn the ropes of a new game or cheer you on while you figure it out.
* **The Library:** We have a solid stash of games ready to play—from quick party favorites to deeper strategy titles.
* **Bring Your Favorites:** Have a game gathering dust on your shelf? Bring it along! We love seeing what the community is playing.
* **The Vibe:** High-quality cider, cozy atmosphere, and just the right amount of competitive spirit.

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

Please see the list below for which parks are open and which parks continue to be closed for safety reasons.OPEN Parks:  Lake Julian Park (please note, some disc golf holes remain closed), Hominy Valley Park, Collier Cove Nature Preserve, North Buncombe Fields, Cane Creek Playground, Buncombe County Sports Park, Corcoran Paige River Park, Bent Creek River Park, Ledges Whitewater Park, and Hominy Creek River Park.  If people choose to recreate on the river, we strongly encourage them to be aware of changes on streambanks and in the riverbed and the potential for unknown debris from Helene.CLOSED Parks:  Charles D. Owen Park, Karpen Soccer Field, Alexander River Park, Walnut Island River Park, and Glen Bridge River Park*. *Note, if the gate is open at Glen Bridge River Park, it may be used.  For safety reasons, we ask the public not to enter closed parks.Please email parks@buncombecounty.org or call (828) 250-4260 with any questions or for additional information.

title: Manifesting Self
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**Location Change:**
**Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**

Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??

Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.

Manifesting Self may sound a little out there. Trust me. It’s not. Whether we’ve been in the remote space for years, since the pandemic, or just recently, I’m certain it has changed each of us in ways we never thought possible. Let’s explore that together. The highs, the lows, and everywhere in between. And from there experience growth.

We are so excited to see you, again or for the first time!

title: Thursday Run
description:
Asheville Runners
Come run 1, 3, or 6 miles and stay for a beer and soccer tennis after at Olde London Road.

Routes-
1 miler:
RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.
RIGHT on River Arts Place
Cross Riverside onto the Greenway
Right on the Greenway to the Craven St Park put in (the dock)
Turn around and go back the same way to OLR

3 miler:
Start the same as 1 miler
Continue onto Craven St. Bridge
LEFT onto Greenway after bridge
Follow Greenway all the way until it ends at Haywood Rd.
RIGHT onto Haywood Rd, go across the bridge
Cross the Roundabout at Roberts St. and continue onto Clingman
Continue on Clingman
LEFT onto Owens Bell Lane
LEFT onto Hilliard at the top of the hill
LEFT onto W Haywood, follow all the way down to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts
Follow Roberts back to OLR
Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

6 miler:
After the W Haywood downhill to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts St. take to Lyman and head back to the Greenway
LEFT onto the Greenway, take all the way to Amboy
RIGHT on Amboy to cross the bridge
RIGHT into French Broad River Park, run the loop at the park
Cross back over the bridge on Amboy and run the Greenway back to the roundabout
Follow Lyman back to OLR

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Evening Group Meditation IN-PERSON or ONLINE
description:
Asheville Meditation Meetup Group
Led by Founding teacher Ronya Banks or AIM Facilitator Wallace Bohanan, our Thursday evening group meditation sessions will continue to consist of a guided meditation (30 minutes), a few-minute break, a dharma talk by the teacher (30 minutes), and then Q & A/Discussion (30 minutes).

Meditation instructions will be given for beginners.

The session begins promptly at 7:00 pm. If online, please mute your audio during the guided meditation and talk.

Location

MindSpring Building
966 Tunnel Road, Asheville, NC 28805

Please Donate ($10 Suggested)

We need your generosity now more than ever before. Please hit the Donate Button to your right and donate whatever you can afford. Or become one of our monthly sustaining donars. (The suggested minimum donation is $10, but no one is turned away for lack of funds.)

Group Meditation Guidelines

* Arrive several minutes early. You are welcome to greet others before we start.
* Turn off your cell phones and other beeping devices.
* Sit in a comfortable position, chairs are provided, bring your own cushions, blankets, or props.
* If on zoom, please mute yourself during guided meditation, and talk, and then unmute yourself to share during the discussion.

title: Game Night @ Archetype Brewing
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**
